newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS - Handelsbanken ups nine-month profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Handelsbanken ups nine-month profit.

text.p: Sweden's top commercial bank, Handelsbanken, on Tuesday reported a 19 percent rise in earnings for the first nine months of the year, boosted by its investment banking operations and higher interest income.
Its profit after loan losses grew to 4.52 billion crowns ($688 million) from 3.79 billion in the same period last year.
Including changes in the value of property taken over, loan losses fell 26 percent to 1.31 billion crowns, 0.6 percent of lending volume. Bad debts fell 28 percent to 2.64 billion.
With loan losses gradually fading into the background, attention has moved further up the profit and loss account to indications of underlying profitability.
Earnings before loan losses showed a less dramatic improvement but were nonetheless a respectable 5.83 billion crowns, compared with 5.56 billion a year earlier.
Investment banking operations and a recovery in the lending market were behind the better top-line performance, the bank said in a statement.

"The net of commission interest and costs increased by 19 percent compared with the same period last year, largely due to high volumes both in share trading and in corporate finance and custodial services," it said.
As interest rates have fallen steadily throughout the year, demand for domestic and business credits has recovered and lending volumes in the Swedish banking system have risen.

In addition, the fact that short-term market rates have fallen further than long bond yields has benefited banks, which tend to cover long lending such as mortgages with borrowing in short-term instruments.

The net contribution from financial transactions was unchanged at 906 million crowns but Handelsbanken said an unrealised capital gain of more than 600 million crowns on its bond portfolio had not been included in the result for the period.

Including this gain, earnings would have been well ahead of market expectations. As it was, market forecasts for a profit after credit losses of 4.52 billion crowns were spot on target and its shares fell 0.5 crown to 161 on a listless stock market.
Handelsbanken's total expenses increased by just five percent, of which two percentage points were attributable to depreciation on leasing operations.
Key ratios remain strong, with capital coverage running at 11.7 percent and the tier one capital ratio at 8.7 percent.

These figures have fallen from 14.2 and 10.3 percent, respectively, reported at the same time last year, a fact which Handelsbanken said was due to the divestment of its Nackebro property unit and higher business volumes.
The report was strong across the board and analysts said the company's mounting cash assets would soon be looking for a home, possibly heralding a long-awaited restructuring of the industry.
"I don't rule out a bid for (mortgage lender) Stadshypotek," one Stockholm-based analyst said.
"They could also use the money to pay a substantial bonus dividend, or failing that, a share buy-back would be very tasty indeed," he added. ($1=6.569 Swedish Crown)
